issue_context.title: `ruff server` should support an optional TOML configuration file
issue_context.body: In addition to common Ruff configuration fields that were introduced in https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/10984, `ruff server` should support a configuration file that can be used to configure the linter and formatter. These will take priority over file-based settings by default, though an option to have file-based settings take priority should also be available to the user.
comments: Shouldn't it simply use the parameters from `~/.config/ruff/ruff.toml` ? Do you plan to introduce a LS specific config file ?
Yeah it will read and support that just like a CLI invocation. But some users will want to point to a specific configuration file, and we want to expose that (e.g.) in the VS Code settings pane.

Ok, this makes perfect sense.
Best of luck with the brand new Rust language server.

review_comments: I'm open to using a better name for this 😅
I think we'll need to expand tildes and environment variables for settings that users provide in VS Code. (We do this within Ruff when you pass `--config`.) Should that happen within the LSP?

I would expect this to be a VS Code extension functionality, except if we support it for `ruff check --config` too. Except if we think that's something that's also useful for neovim (does neovim support expanding environment variables). 

Relevant issue https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-vscode/issues/448

Environment variable resolution is definitely something we should have, but I think that's beyond the scope of this PR. As for tilde resolution - shouldn't that be resolved already in `parse_pyproject_toml`?

Okay, I did some testing and it looks like tilde expansion isn't handled by the standard library automatically. I'll open a follow-up PR that uses `shellexpand` to expand tildes and environment variables.
